description: The CFG-based taint engine does not fire ReDoS findings on canonical vulnerable patterns when the regex is a literal (no string interpolation). Verified: test/samples/vulnerable_patterns.cr contains Regex.new('(a+)+') and Regex.new('([a-zA-Z]+)*'). CFG engine: 0 findings. Flat engine: 2 findings. Same divergence as the substring-match FP class, but the root cause is different — likely that the CFG engine's transfer_node for ILCall only flags Regex.new when the result is assigned to a tainted LVal (interpolation_tainted path on cfg_taint.ml:~90-100). For a standalone Regex.new literal call, there is no taint flow, so the call never reaches check_call_sinks. Likely fix: in transfer_node for ILCall, when the callee is a known taint-irrelevant sink shape (e.g. Regex.new with a literal arg), still route through check_call_sinks with a synthetic tainted-args=false state so the rule's check_args_contain condition can fire. Verify post-fix: scanning vulnerable_patterns.cr in CFG mode should produce >= 2 ReDoS findings (matching flat engine). Pre-existing gap, not introduced by any prior fix.

comments.text:
Status: partial — main fix NOT shipped. The single-line fix to cfg_taint.ml:291 (the early-return guard for pattern-only rules) is correct in principle and unblocks ReDoS in the CFG engine, but it also surfaces a separate divergence: the flat engine has a file-wide timeout-setter check (file_has_timeout_setters) that suppresses MissingTimeout findings when the same file contains read_timeout=/connect_timeout=/write_timeout= calls. The CFG engine lacks this check, so the line 291 fix introduces 3 NEW MissingTimeout FPs on test/samples/safe_timeouts.cr (net negative). Reverted.

Two pre-existing bugs must be fixed before this ticket can be fully resolved:
1. Crystal hierarchical mapper's parse_top_level_exprs labels top-level constant assignments as IUnknown and drops them, so test/samples/vulnerable_patterns.cr's EVIL_REGEX = Regex.new("(a+)+") never reaches the IL. (Engine fix at of_catseye_ast.ml walk_item is not enough; the mapper itself is the bottleneck for Crystal.)
2. CFG engine lacks the file-wide timeout-setter check that the flat engine has in interpreter.ml:286-289. The proper fix ports that check to the CFG engine (e.g. walk all functions in the file for timeout-setter calls before emitting the early-return).

One small fix did ship as a separate commit: walk_item now processes IConstant items (commit f9fe1cf). This is a no-op for the existing test suite but helps future OCaml 'let _ = <expr>' expressions reach the CFG engine.

title: CFG engine does not detect ReDoS in non-interpolated patterns
